title: Phased termination of legacy sync-embed endpoint and migration PRD
creator: Asha Rao
description: Background: We currently support a legacy sync /embed endpoint (legacy-sync-embed) dating from early product iterations. This endpoint uses a different batching contract, fixed model aliasing (model_v0_embed), and a synchronous request/response contract that bypasses new quota/telemetry hooks. Problem: maintaining two parallel embed transports increases operational cost, skews token billing telemetry, and prevents us from enabling new batching/kv-cache optimizations for embeddings workloads. Goal: decommission legacy-sync-embed in a phased, low-risk manner while providing clear migration tooling, SDK adapters, billing parity guarantees, and enterprise SLAs for affected customers. Success metrics: (1) 95% of active callers migrated or on a migration plan before termination, (2) less than 0.5% increase in P1 incidents related to embedding failures during rollout, (3) billing parity validated for top 20 customers within the first 30 days of migration staging.
acceptance_criteria: Define and publish a migration compatibility guide and command-line migration assistant that rewrites legacy sync-embed calls to the unified /embeddings generate API

Provide an official SDK adapter (Python + Node) that preserves older request semantics (sync blocking behavior) but calls the unified async endpoint with transparent polling so clients require minimal changes
Telemetry and billing parity: token/embedding-unit accounting for migrated calls must match prior invoices within 2% for top 20 customers tested against synthetic workloads
Operational guardrails: circuit-breaker and fallback to a designated dedicated capacity pool for enterprise customers during traffic ramp-down
Rollout gating: automated telemetry gates (error rate, latency p95, token delta) must be green for 72 hours in shadow mode before each phased cutover
Customer communication: targeted emails and in-console banners delivered to all impacted API keys with migration instructions and deadlines at least 60 and 30 days prior to termination
Rollback criteria and post-mortem: documented rollback steps and mandatory post-mortem for any production incident exceeding Severity 2 during the migration window
scope: In scope: deprecation and removal of legacy-sync-embed endpoint, SDK adapters (Python and Node), migration CLI, billing reconciliation scripts, telemetry gates, enterprise migration SLAs and a phased cutover plan. Create Console banners and usage export for impacted customers. Coordinate with legal on contract addenda where needed.
out_of_scope: Out of scope: changes to embedding model architectures, on-prem private deployments requiring custom offline adapters (handled by Private team as a separate engagement), or wholesale changes to embedding billing model beyond parity reconciliation adjustments.
migration_steps: Inventory: produce an export of keys and apps calling legacy-sync-embed (usage > 0 in last 90 days)
Build: implement SDK adapter libs that map legacy payload to unified /embeddings generate and preserve blocking semantics
Shadow testing: enable shadow-routing for 25% of traffic with telemetry comparisons and billing simulation for top customers
CLI release: publish migration assistant CLI and step-by-step guide in Confluence and Console docs
Engage customers: send targeted migration emails, offer 1:1 migration slots for enterprise customers, and provide a temporary dedicated capacity pool for high-volume clients
Phased cutover: close new legacy keys in waves by account tier (P0 customers preserved until migration plan signed), final shutdown after a 30-day drainage window
Post-termination: run billing reconciliation and open customer support window for one-off disputes
rollout_timeline: Week 0-2: Inventory, comms drafting, SDK adapter alpha. Week 3-6: Shadow tests and billing sims with 5 pilot customers. Week 7-10: Expand shadow to 25-50% traffic, fix regressions. Week 11-14: Open migration assistance, staged key closures by tier. Week 15: Final termination and 30-day dispute window. Target final shutdown date: 2025-06-01 (subject to gating).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Unexpected token billing delta for high-cardinality requests could trigger customer disputes — Mitigation: run synthetic replay against historical footprints and offer one-time bill credits during migration
Risk: SDK adapter introduces edge-case latency regressions — Mitigation: benchmark adapter in CI, keep adapter as opt-in until telemetry gates pass 72h
Risk: Some enterprise on-prem customers cannot accept remote migration timelines — Mitigation: offer a Private deployment patch/backport plan and negotiate contract addenda
Risk: Shadow routing masks production-only bug — Mitigation: include canary accounts with real traffic and staged burst tests under peak load
notes: 02-15 Review: ENG requested an extra 3 weeks for kernel-level batching compatibility testing — accommodated in timeline
02-18 Legal: require a short addendum for enterprise customers under legacy SLAs — PM to coordinate templates
02-20 Design: console banner copy must include one-click 'Request migration help' action linked to a calendar booking flow
02-24 QA: flagged two request shapes that drop metadata headers during adapter translation; ENG to resolve before public SDK publish
